lessonRef.title: Synthesis and review: resolving a billing error or dispute

focus: resolving a billing error or dispute
objective: Separate unauthorised charges from a merchant billing error on a simulated card statement, compute what is genuinely owed, and route each category to the right remedy.
scenario: The simulated card statement below and every charge on it are fictional. No real card, account, or merchant is involved, and no card details appear anywhere in this lesson.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional statement summary in these directions

tasks.directions: The simulated statement totals $1,247.83. It includes two charges the cardholder did not make and does not recognise, for $318.40 and $96.75. It also includes a charge of $54.00 from a merchant the cardholder did use, billed twice for one purchase. The rest of the statement is charges the cardholder made and accepts. Interest runs at 1.65% a month on any balance carried, except that while an amount is formally in dispute the fictional issuer charges no interest on it and does not treat it as late.

prompts.text: What do the two unrecognised charges come to?
What is the total of everything the cardholder should not have to pay?
What is genuinely owed on this statement?

tasks.directions: Now route each category and price the delay.

prompts.text: Which of the disputed amounts should be reported to the card issuer as charges the cardholder did not make, rather than taken up with a merchant first?
If the disputed $469.15 were carried on the card for one month at 1.65% rather than being disputed, what would the interest be?
The card issuer’s minimum payment for the month is $35. Does the genuinely owed amount exceed it?
choices: Yes — the owed amount is well above the minimum
No — the minimum is larger than what is owed

prompts.text: Two problems on one statement need two different responses. Explain why the $415.15 and the $54.00 are not the same kind of problem, say what each response should be, and name one action the cardholder should take about the $415.15 that has nothing to do with this statement.

remediation: If the amount owed comes out as $832.68, only the unauthorised charges have been removed and the $54.00 duplicate is still in the total. Take out everything the cardholder should not pay — $318.40, $96.75, and $54.00 — to reach $778.68, and keep the two categories labelled separately, because they go to different places.
extension: Work out what the interest would come to if the disputed $469.15 stayed on the card for 4 months, and say what that implies about how quickly an unauthorised charge should be reported.
